sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the west side of Glassboro's downtown, centred on West High Street, which crosses the sheet from left to right. North of High Street are two large blocks divided by North Lake Street: the western block, between Cedar Street and North Lake, is cut into a dense run of narrow residential lots, mostly vacant, with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings; the eastern block, between North Lake and North Poplar, holds a row of dwellings along North Lake and the Glassboro High School, a large brick building with an attached kindergarten and a separate classroom building behind it. West New Street runs along the top of the sheet, with a 6 inch water pipe in it. South of High Street the blocks are smaller and more built up, mainly two-storey dwellings with cinder block stores along High Street. Ellis Street runs diagonally to the lower left and meets Railroad Avenue and Church Street at a skewed junction. Railroad Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet beside the tracks of the W. J. & S. R.R. and the P.R.R., with S. Lake and S. Poplar Streets crossing them. Water pipes and dwelling numbers are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its north arrow turned about 13 degrees from vertical, and the left edge and upper left corner are left blank as parts of adjoining sheets 14 and 7.
notes: South Lake Street is now Fred Tartaglione Street (OpenStreetMap); North Lake no longer appears in OpenStreetMap.
West High Street is now High Street; South Poplar Street is now Poplar Street South; North Poplar Street has been replaced by the Rowan Boulevard area.

Railroad Avenue and the W. J. & S. R.R. corridor west of South Lake Street is now Oakwood Avenue; the Fred Tartaglione Street / Oakwood Avenue junction was excluded because the drawn Railroad Avenue centre is about 6 m from the modern node.
Downtown west of Main: N. Lake, N./S. Poplar, W. High, Ellis, Cedar, Victoria, W. New, Railroad Av; 50 ft. Fred Tartaglione / Oakwood junction excluded (tracks in the old Railroad Av).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 is the commercial centre of Glassboro, built around the crossing of Main Street and High Street. North Main Street and South Main Street run down the middle of the sheet, West High Street and East High Street cross them near the bottom, and College Street crosses the upper middle between North Main and Center Streets and runs on to North Academy Street at the right edge. North Poplar and South Poplar Streets run along the left side, West New and East New Streets along the top, and Railroad Avenue with the W. J. & S. R.R. and P.R.R. tracks along the bottom left. Along High Street are the pink and blue business blocks, including the First National Bank, the post office, a municipal hall, the Glassboro Title and Trust Co., the Glassboro Public Works with a jail, and the Borough of Glassboro Water Works pump house, beside rows of cinder block stores. North of High Street are a fire department, a paint store with a hall, a pool room, an auto house and a shirt factory. The upper blocks hold dwellings, with the First M.E. Church at the top right, and a curved A.C.R.R. and P. & R. Ry. siding crosses the lower right. The Glassboro Highway Department yard is at the bottom centre. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the north arrow tilted about 6 degrees to the left.
notes: West High Street is High Street and East High Street is East High Street in OpenStreetMap; North Main and South Main are North Main Street and South Main Street; College is College Avenue; North Academy and South Academy are Academy Street North and Academy Street South.
South Poplar Street is Poplar Street South; North Poplar Street no longer exists, the area being occupied by Rowan Boulevard and the university.
West New and East New Street jog at North Main Street; the modern New Street node there is not a drawn junction and was excluded.
The Glassboro Highway Dept., Borough of Glassboro Water Works Pump House and Glassboro Public Works are marked; the water works carries a note See Report Sheet No. 1.

Downtown: N./S. Main, W./E. High, College, Center, N./S. Academy, N./S. Poplar, W./E. New, Railroad Av; 50 ft. Pilot sheet. N. Poplar and College west of Main replaced by Rowan Boulevard redevelopment; W. New / E. New jog at Main (junction excluded).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the east side of Glassboro's downtown along East High Street and State Road. North Academy Street runs down the left edge of the sheet and meets East High Street at the lower left, where South Academy Street continues south. State Road runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right and joins North Broad Street at the lower right corner, forming a long triangular district between it, North Academy and East High Street. Along North Academy Street are dwellings, the Glassboro Public School (a large building of non-fireproof brick drawn in blue), the Glassboro Enterprise printing shop, A. A. Weisner Monuments, the parish house of St. Thomas Episcopal Church and a telephone office. The block between State Road and East High Street holds a single row of dwellings fronting State Road, large open lots, the Shaw-Paulin American Legion Post, and near the lower right a hat factory and a small shop. Liberty Street, with a 4 inch water pipe, enters from the east near North Broad Street. Warrick Street and Williams Street run south from East High Street at the bottom. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, the north arrow points almost straight up, and the margins are blank, with adjoining sheets 3, 5, 8, 18 and 20 named at the edges.
notes: East High Street, North Academy and South Academy are Academy Street North, Academy Street South and East High Street in OpenStreetMap; Warrick Street is Warrick Avenue.
State Road is State Street in OpenStreetMap, and North Broad Street is Delsea Drive (North).
Placed by three hand-picked points along East High Street (helmert fit); the detector found only two junctions and measured them 14 ft off the hand reading, so the part is low confidence.
E. High, Warrick, Williams, N./S. Academy, State Rd, N. Broad, Liberty, E. New; 50 ft. Low confidence: helmert on three hand-picked points along East High Street.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows North Broad Street, which runs down the middle of the sheet, and the blocks on both sides of it between East New Street at the top and Liberty Street at the bottom. State Road runs diagonally along the left side of the sheet and the narrow wedge between State Road and North Broad Street is lined with dwellings on deep lots, with a few garages and a frame store building. Cross Keys Road runs across the top right, and an unnamed street marked as not named crosses the middle of the sheet to the right of North Broad Street. Wright Street is drawn at the top as not opened. East of North Broad Street the lots are mostly large vacant blocks numbered 115 and 116, with dwellings and a cinder block building at the north end; at the lower end an auto showroom and repair garage with a boiler room, drawn in blue as non-fireproof brick, stands on North Broad Street near Liberty Street, and east of it a row of long narrow vacant lots runs along Liberty Street. Water pipes of 4 inches are drawn in North Broad, Liberty and Cross Keys Road. The right edge of the sheet carries the words No Exposure. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the north arrow points about 17 degrees to the right of vertical.
notes: North Broad Street is Delsea Drive in OpenStreetMap; State Road is State Street.
Cross Keys Road is probably Gifford Street in OpenStreetMap, but the detector measured that junction on a lot line, so it was excluded.
Placed from a single hand-picked junction (Delsea Drive / Liberty Street) plus a derived point 300 ft north at the atlas scale; low confidence, rotation taken from the north arrow.

E. New, Cross Keys Rd, Wright, N. Broad (Delsea Drive), State Rd, Liberty; 50 ft. Low confidence: anchored on Delsea / Liberty with rotation from the compass; Delsea Drive is displaced against old Broad Street (see sheet 18).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 is drawn turned, with its north arrow pointing up and to the right at roughly 30 degrees, so the streets run diagonally across the page. It covers the district north of New Street on both sides of North Main Street, which crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right. West of North Main Street, North Lake Street, Eben Street and West West Street are laid out as a grid of long blocks between West New Street and the top of the sheet, filled with dwellings and their outbuildings on narrow lots, with a few blue non-fireproof structures and a pink building used as a school or hall near the middle. East of North Main Street, a wedge-shaped district lies between East New Street, North Main Street and State Road, holding dwellings, a movie theatre on North Main Street near the New Street junction, and a row of dwellings along State Road. East West Street meets North Main Street and State Road at the upper right. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along most streets. Adjoining sheets 2, 3, 14 and 19 are named at the margins. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: North Main Street keeps its name; West New and East New Street are both New Street (New Street West further west); West West Street and East West Street are West Street.
State Road is State Street in OpenStreetMap; North Lake, Eben and North Poplar Street are not in OpenStreetMap here.
Only three junctions were found, with residuals of 5 to 8 m against the three-point fit; low confidence.
North of New St: N. Lake, Eben, W. West, N. Main, W./E. New, N. Poplar, State Rd; 50 ft, turned about 33 degrees. Low confidence: three points.

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 7 is the main map, covering the area south of Railroad Avenue and the Glassboro rail line on both sides of South Main Street. South Lake Street and South Poplar Street run north to south across the upper left and centre, meeting Wilmer Street, which crosses the sheet from left to right and bends at the lower left where Wilmer Street continues diagonally toward Church Street. Church Street runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, ending at Union Street at the bottom right. South Main Street runs down the right side of the sheet, with a 6 inch water pipe along it. At the top, Railroad Avenue carries the W. J. & S. R.R. and P.R.R. tracks, a siding curving to a freight station with a wooden platform, and south of it are blocks of dwellings with frame outbuildings and stables, a cinder block storage building, and two coops. South of Wilmer Street are rows of dwellings and a rectory, the Methodist Protestant Church, a cemetery, and a fire-resistive dwelling in blue. The heavy black line at the lower left separates this part from part 2, a block drawn displaced at the same scale and rotation. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the north arrow tilted slightly to the left.
notes: South Lake Street is now Fred Tartaglione Street; South Poplar Street is Poplar Street South; South Main Street keeps its name.
Church Street and Wilmer Street keep their names; Railroad Avenue with the W. J. & S. R.R. corridor west of South Lake is now Oakwood Avenue.
The block left of the heavy line is part 2 and is drawn elsewhere on the ground.

S. Lake (now Fred Tartaglione Street), S. Poplar, S. Main, Wilmer, Church, Union, Railroad Av (W. J. & S. R.R., corridor now Oakwood Avenue); 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 (below and left of the heavy line) the block west of S. Lake between Railroad Av and Church, drawn displaced at the same scale and rotation, placed from two points carried from part 1.

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 7 is the lower-left block below the heavy black line, drawn at the same scale and rotation as part 1 but standing on the ground at a different place. It shows the block between Railroad Avenue, South Lake Street and Church Street west of South Lake Street. Railroad Avenue crosses the upper part diagonally with the tracks of the W. J. & S. R.R. and P.R.R., and a few small dwellings and business buildings stand on its north side beside Ellis Street at the upper left. South of the railroad a triangular block lies between Church Street, which runs diagonally from the upper left, and South Lake Street at the right, with the lots numbered 50 and 114 and facing Church Street. The block holds frame dwellings with outbuildings, a building marked St. Anthony Society, an ice cream factory in blue at the lower end and a small blue dwelling. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches follow Church Street and South Lake Street, and the sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheets adjoining at the edges are 2, 7 and 16.
notes: South Lake Street is now Fred Tartaglione Street; Church Street and Ellis Street keep their names.
Railroad Avenue and the W. J. & S. R.R. corridor here is now Oakwood Avenue.
Sheet 2 also draws Ellis Street, Railroad Avenue and Church Street at its lower left corner.

S. Lake (now Fred Tartaglione Street), S. Poplar, S. Main, Wilmer, Church, Union, Railroad Av (W. J. & S. R.R., corridor now Oakwood Avenue); 50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map; part 2 (below and left of the heavy line) the block west of S. Lake between Railroad Av and Church, drawn displaced at the same scale and rotation, placed from two points carried from part 1.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the blocks south of East High Street on both sides of South Academy Street, running down the middle-right of the sheet, with South Main Street along the left edge. At the top, East High Street carries a large pink brick building labelled as a movie theatre with a lobby, balcony and pilastered walls, with a note that concrete foundations only are drawn and work is abandoned for the adjoining ground. Long narrow residential lots line South Academy Street on its west side and South Main Street on its east side, mostly with dwellings and small outbuildings; an undertaker's shop, a W.C.T.U. hall and a coal and fuel yard are marked. A railroad line, the A.C.R.R. and P. & R. Ry., runs north to south through the middle of the sheet between the two streets, with a branch of the W. J. & S. R.R. entering from the left near the top; a siding curves toward the centre. East of South Academy Street the blocks 245 and 246 are divided into many narrow vacant lots, bounded by Grillo Street, Messina Street (not opened) and Warrick Street, with the east side of Warrick Street marked not opened further south. At the bottom left are D. L. Schaible's coal, feed and builders' supplies and the Glassboro Fuel Service coal yard is at the top left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the north arrow tilted about 10 degrees to the left.
notes: South Academy Street is Academy Street South in OpenStreetMap; East High Street and Warrick are East High Street and Warrick Avenue; Messina is marked not opened.
Grillo Street / Messina Street and Grillo Street / Warrick Avenue are two modern nodes about 1 m apart at one drawn junction; Messina Street was left out of the street list.
The A.C.R.R. and P. & R. Ry. line through the middle of the sheet has no modern OpenStreetMap counterpart used here.
S. Academy, Grillo, Messina (not opened), Warrick, S. Main, Wilmer, D. L. Schaible coal yard; 50 ft. Messina left out (same junction as Grillo/Warrick in OpenStreetMap).

sheet-9.description: The part shows the east side of Glassboro between Wilmer Street along the top and Union Street at the lower right, with Church Street forming the right edge. Two blocks of mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings face Wilmer Street and Zane Street, drawn in yellow on narrow lots; the larger lots on Zane Street hold a greenhouse and an A.M.E. church with its rectory. At the left, East Avenue runs along the edge of a railroad right of way, and the heavy double line of a railroad crosses diagonally from the left centre to the foot of the sheet, where it meets Union Street. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in Wilmer, Zane and Church streets. The lower half is largely open ground and unbuilt lots. A compass rose with its north arrow lies at the lower left, and the sheet is turned so that north points up and to the right. Adjoining sheets 16, 17, 7 and 10 are referenced by number around the edges.
notes: Streets are lettered without suffixes except East Av. and Franklin St.
Wilmer Street, Zane Street, Church Street, Union Street and Franklin Street keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
Control is weak: only the junctions on Church Street and a hand-picked pipe junction at Franklin and Wilmer.
Church, Wilmer, Zane, Union, East Av, Franklin; 50 ft. Low confidence: three points, fitted scale 4 percent high.

sheet-10.description: The part covers the south end of Glassboro's centre around South Main Street, Union Street and East and West Grove streets. In the upper half the Pennsylvania and Reading and the Atlantic City railroad lines (the Williamstown Branch) run in from the north and split in a wye, crossing the sheet east to west near the middle. Near the top are the grain house and a coal, feed and builders supplies yard, and the Glassboro station and freight house stand beside the tracks. Church Street runs diagonally from the upper left. Houses and the Bethlehem Reform Church and the Pilgrim Holiness Church front South Main Street, and the Peoples Gas Company service building and garage stands below the tracks. The lower part shows East Grove Street running to the right with the West Jersey and Seashore track alongside, a vacant building at the west end, and long deep lots on both sides. South Academy Street runs down at the right, with Messina and Diaz streets at the upper right. A 6 and 8 inch water pipe is marked in most streets.
notes: Only two automatic control points, both on Grove Street, so the placement is helmert (low confidence).
South Main Street, East and West Grove, South Academy Street are Main Street, Grove Street and Academy Street South in OpenStreetMap.
Printed names of Messina Street and Diaz Street were read from the overview.
S. Main, E./W. Grove, Union, Church, S. Academy, Messina and Diaz St. at the margin, rail wye and freight station, Peoples Gas Co. garage; 50 ft. Low confidence: helmert on two Grove Street points.

sheet-12.description: The part shows Chestnut Ridge Estates, a gridded subdivision on the west side of Glassboro drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Mullica Hill Road crosses the top, with Hecton Road at the upper left, and University Boulevard crosses the middle. Between them the cross streets Hamilton, Swarthmore, Villa Nova, Dickinson and Georgetown roads run east and west, and Lehigh, Harvard, Yale and Columbia roads run north and south. The blocks are numbered and cut into long narrow lots, and only a minority of lots hold houses, so most of the area is unbuilt. Several streets are marked not opened. The First Presbyterian Church stands on University Boulevard. Girard Road and the railroad cross the upper right corner. Water pipes of 4 inches are marked in the streets, and the sheet edges carry the legend No Exposure. The lettering Chestnut Ridge Estates is spread across the sheet.
notes: Villa Nova Road is Villanova Road in OpenStreetMap; Hamilton, Swarthmore and Dickinson roads match.
Columbia Road North and South are displaced about 13 m from the drawn line and were left out of the fit.
Names were read from the overview and not on full-resolution crops; the printed W. West at the top right is uncertain.

Chestnut Ridge Estates grid: Mullica Hill Rd, Georgetown Rd, University Blvd, Hamilton, Swarthmore, Villa Nova, Dickinson, Lehigh, Harvard, Yale; 100 ft. Columbia Road left out (about 13 m off its drawn line).

sheet-13.description: The part shows the New Jersey State Normal School and the railroad corner of Glassboro, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. A wide diagonal band of the Pennsylvania and Reading and West Jersey and Seashore railroads crosses from the upper left to the lower right, with Girard Road alongside. The school group at the centre has an auditorium with gym and stage, a green house and the dormitories to the east, each marked with its construction. Railroad Avenue and Whitney Avenue meet at the Glassboro station at the right, with W. High Street and Victoria Street at the upper right, and Franklin Street leads off the lower right. The left side holds the western part of Chestnut Ridge Estates: University Boulevard, Dickinson, Georgetown and Villa Nova roads, Princeton and Columbia roads and Pennsylvania Road, with houses on part of the lots. West Street runs along the top as a 50 foot street. A north arrow at the upper left is turned to the east.
notes: Villa Nova Road is Villanova Road in OpenStreetMap; Whitney Avenue and Railroad Avenue are not in the extract as such.
Columbia Road is displaced about 13 m and was left out of the fit.
Names were read from the overview and not on full-resolution crops.
New Jersey State Normal School, Girard Rd, Georgetown Rd, University Blvd, Pennsylvania and Princeton Rds, rail; 100 ft. Columbia Road South left out (13.5 m).

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the western edge of Glassboro, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees from the usual orientation, with a north arrow at upper left. A wedge-shaped area is bounded by the street lettered W. West along the top, the diagonal railroad right-of-way crossing the sheet from lower left to upper right, and Railroad Avenue along the bottom, where the railroad tracks run. Within the wedge lie rows of narrow lots and scattered frame dwellings (yellow) along W. New, Victoria, W. High, Holly, Cedar, Whitney Av. and Ellis, with Eben Place and an unnamed lane at the north. Block numbers 101 to 111 and 229, 230 and 244 mark the blocks. Several blocks are shown only as outlined lots with no buildings. At upper left, the New Jersey State Normal School grounds are drawn sparsely: a pink-coloured brick building at the left margin, a hospital-like group of blue and yellow buildings near the centre and a few outbuildings, with the school's campus roads not yet shown. At upper right a laundry (Day Light Laundry) and a lumber yard group stand along N. Lake and W. West, with a stretch of undeveloped parcels. Abbott Bros. works appears at top centre. Adjoining sheets are indicated by the numbers 13, 16, 19, 6 and 2 at the margins. The scale bar is at the bottom. The lower part is mostly open land crossed by lot lines.
notes: Modern names: West New Street is New Street West; Victoria Street is Victoria Avenue; Cedar is Cedar Avenue and, north of Victoria, Mick Drive; West High Street is High Street.
Names were read from reduced crops; spellings and abbreviations should be checked against the full-resolution sheet (medium confidence).
Normal School east, W. West, N. Lake, Cedar, Eben Pl, W. New, Victoria, Holly, Whitney Av, W. High; 100 ft, turned about -20 degrees.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the Chestnut Ridge Estates and Glassboro Estates subdivisions south-west of the town centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the north arrow points down-left. The upper two thirds is a regular plan of long narrow lots between Georgetown Rd. along the top, then Franklin, Cornell and Deptford roads, cut by Columbia, Princeton and Girard roads, with Pennsylvania Rd. running diagonally at the left. Almost all of the lots are vacant; a scatter of small dwellings, mostly frame, stands on a few of them, chiefly along Franklin Rd. and Princeton Rd. and near Girard Rd. Block numbers (6, 7, 8, 19, 20, 21 and others) identify the lots, and the tract name is lettered across the blocks. Below Deptford Rd. the sheet is mostly open land with a compass rose, crossed by the diagonal line of Ellis and a railroad. Near Sewell at the right edge stand the buildings of J. J. Farley Co. Inc. and, in the lower right corner, the works of Alunite Products Inc., with a few dwellings between. The bottom edge shows the Glassboro Estates plan with Lovers Lane, Pershing Drive, Roosevelt Lane, Delaware Av. and Lincoln Blvd., none of which was built up. Neighbouring sheets are indicated by the numbers 12, 13, 16 and 17 at the margins.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows the area immediately south-west of the centre of Glassboro, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that its streets run diagonally across the page. Railroad Av. and Church lie along the top; Franklin crosses the upper left, and a second Franklin runs diagonally through the north-eastern blocks beside Ellis and Wilmer. A broad band of railroad tracks, labelled as a bundle of tracks, crosses the middle of the sheet from the left edge to the right, with a station-like building and an electric substation (coloured pink) on the north side. The upper third is the most built-up part: small frame dwellings in blocks numbered 52 and 100, a few shops and the Franklin Mfg. Co. works at the left. Further south, Ellis and Wilmer carry scattered dwellings, a small group of buildings near Ellis is labelled as a refining or manufacturing company, and blocks 99, 119, 120, 160 and 161 are largely undeveloped, with long narrow lots laid out along Wilmer, East Av. and Zane. Center Av. is drawn as a street marked 'not opened'. Sewell runs across the foot of the sheet, with a 6 inch water pipe, a railroad spur and the edge of block 11 (pink buildings). At the left edge Girard Rd., Cornell Rd., Franklin Rd. and Deptford Rd. appear where they meet the tracks. Adjoining sheets are numbered 13, 14, 15, 17, 7, 9 and 11 at the margins.
notes: Center Av. is lettered 'not opened'.
Ellis junctions carry residuals of 3 to 4 m in the fit; the modern Ellis Street may be offset from the drawn line.
Names were read from reduced crops (medium confidence); small lettering at the left edge and in the title block was not checked at full resolution.
Sewell, Franklin, Ellis, Church, Wilmer, Zane, Railroad Av, Girard Rd, rail; 100 ft, turned about -38 degrees. Ellis Street junctions 3 to 4 m out.

sheet-17-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 17 is the upper and eastern portion of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, bounded at lower left by a heavy line that encloses the separately drawn Glassboro Estates subdivision. At the top the Peoples Gas Co. works occupies a large site with gas holders, a retort house and associated buildings, beside a pair of railroad lines running north-west to south-east across the sheet. W. Grove and E. Grove cross below the gas works, and a cluster of small frame dwellings lines the streets east of the tracks near Union and Main. Further south the part is laid out in long narrow lots: Glassboro Av. and Sewell run west to east across the middle, crossed by Highland Av. at the left, with Union and Main running down the right side. Dwellings are scattered and widely spaced; the lots in the interior and at the lower middle (blocks 154, 163 and 13) are mostly empty. At the upper left Zane enters from the margin. The foot of the part includes the plant of Alunite Products Inc. along the heavy line, and a north arrow marks the Glassboro Estates part. Block numbers 9, 10, 11, 59, 154, 159 and 160 are marked, and neighbouring sheets are numbered 16, 20 and 15 at the margins. A scale bar and a library stamp occupy the lower right.
notes: Modern names: Highland Av. is Falcon Avenue; W. Grove and E. Grove are Grove Street.
Names were read from reduced crops (medium confidence).

sheet-18-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 18 is the main portion of the sheet, covering the south-eastern edge of Glassboro at 100 feet to an inch, with a north arrow and compass rose at upper right pointing nearly straight up. A heavy line at the upper left encloses the separately drawn block along Delsea Drive, Green Tree Rd., Spencer Av. and Stanger Av. In this part, E. High runs down from the top across the north-east, with Williams, Warrick and S. Broad running roughly north to south below it. Grillo and Messina (both marked not opened) and Diaz are laid out as long narrow streets across the middle, where blocks 247, 248, 249 and 250 are largely empty. Dwellings are scattered along E. High, Williams and S. Broad, with a church or hall near Williams and a few brick-coloured buildings. A railroad crosses the sheet from left to right below the middle, passing the works of the Central Atlantic States Service Corporation at lower right, which are drawn as large brown and pink buildings with the company's description printed beside them. E. Grove runs along the lower part, with dwellings and a few small buildings; the area below is blank, marked as vacant fields. S. Academy runs down the left edge. Block numbers 4, 8, 10, 27 and 215 are marked, and neighbouring sheets are numbered 17, 19 and 20 at the margins.
notes: Modern names: S. Broad is Delsea Drive; E. High is East High Street; E. Grove is Grove Street.
Grillo and Messina are lettered 'not opened'.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the northern end of Glassboro along N. Main and N. Broad streets, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with a north arrow at right pointing nearly straight up. The two streets run north from the centre of the sheet, converging toward the top, with Carpenter running diagonally in from the upper left and Normal Blvd. along the top-left edge. N. Main carries a continuous line of small frame dwellings, with a few stores near W. West and E. West and a pink-coloured building, the Franklin Hotel, at their junction. Focer crosses the sheet at its middle, with St. Thomas Episcopal Church to the south of it on N. Main. East of N. Broad stands the Glassboro High School, a large brick-coloured building with an auditorium, gymnasium and boys' gymnasium, labelled with its construction. A cemetery lies to its south-east. At the top, a vacant block, a cinder block works and a water tank with an elevated steel frame stand between N. Main and N. Broad, with Stanger Av. and Pomono Av. running east from N. Broad. Blocks numbered 31, 32, 55, 56, 107, 108, 208 and 231 are marked. The lower part shows W. West and E. West, State Rd. branching south-east, E. New, McClelland, Wright (marked 'not opened') and Cross Keys Rd. Dwellings are small and widely spaced, and the area west of N. Main and south-east of State Rd. is largely open land. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 14, 18, 5 and 6 at the margins.
notes: Modern names: N. Broad is Delsea Drive; Pomono Av. is Pomona Avenue; W. West and E. West are West Street; Normal Blvd. is Normal Boulevard.
Names were read from reduced crops (medium confidence); the short word near W. West at the left edge and the abbreviation after McClelland were not read.

sheet-20-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 20 is the western and northern portion of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, bounded on the south-east by a heavy line that separates it from a second block drawn at a different orientation. N. Broad and S. Broad run down the left edge, with Liberty crossing at the top and State St. entering at the upper left. E. High runs diagonally south-east from N. Broad across the middle of the part, lined with small frame dwellings on narrow lots, many with their lot letters marked; Reading runs north-east from E. High towards Liberty. Block numbers 26, 116, 162 and 167 are marked. South of E. High, S. Broad carries a continuous row of dwellings on its east side, with a few brick-coloured or blue buildings, while the interior blocks are open. At the lower left, E. Grove St. meets S. Broad beside the plant of Repp Orchard Products Co. (steam power, lights and water supply noted on the sheet), a group of buildings including a bottling works, with the railroad (Wilmington branch of the Atlantic City railroad) passing by it. The Keogh Canning Factory stands to the east of the plant, and the Voelker Bros. Torpedo Mfg. (marked not in operation) lies below the heavy line at the foot. A north arrow and compass rose at the top right point nearly straight up. The upper right is mostly blank, marked no exposure.
notes: Modern names: N. Broad and S. Broad are Delsea Drive; E. High is East High Street; Liberty is Liberty Street.

Only three hand-picked points, all on Delsea Drive, control this part (helmert, low confidence); they lie along one line, so rotation and scale are poorly fixed. Names were read from reduced crops (medium confidence).

sheet-20-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 20 is the block south-east of the heavy line that crosses the sheet, in the south-east of Glassboro. It is bounded on the west by South Main Street, with the W. J. & S. R.R. running alongside it, and on the east by South Academy Street; Oak Street crosses the part from east to west, and East Avenue runs north from Oak Street between the railroad and Academy. The area is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings with outbuildings and coops along Academy Street, Oak Street and East Avenue, a track of the railroad on a wooden trestle running into the lots west of East Avenue, and large vacant lots, numbered 14 and 166, in the middle and south of the part. The lower edge is marked no exposure and vacant fields. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north straight up, a different angle from part 1 of the sheet, whose main map shows High, Reading and Broad Streets west and north of the heavy line. Blocks along its edges are drawn in full on the neighbouring sheets 10, 17 and 18, whose numbers are printed at the margins. The upper part of the block, north of the trestle, is mostly empty ground, and the few buildings shown are small dwellings, stores and sheds rather than works; the larger industrial sites of this end of town, the Keogh canning factory and the Voelker torpedo works, lie on the other side of the heavy line in part 1.
